routing_rule: repair = HIGH/MEDIUM that violates acceptance, reddens the gate, or makes a published number/claim dishonest; everything else -> debt regardless of severity

findings.claim: `demo_ready` / `infrastructure_failures` / the printed "N/N completed without an infrastructure failure" count a run that never got off the ground (`failure:env`) as a clean completion, so a soak against a deployment whose planner cannot start publishes a green demo-readiness verdict.
findings.evidence: evals/soak.py:171-178 — `completed = [r for r in rows if not r.get("transport_error")]` and `demo_ready = not infra and len(completed) == len(rows)`; `transport_error` is only ever set on the four client-side phases, so a terminal record {"status": "failure:env", "reason": "planner failed: RuntimeError: OPENROUTER_API_KEY not set"} is a "completion". soak.py:140 already computes `measured=is_measurement(...)` which is False for exactly these rows, and nothing aggregates it. D20 (docs/support-matrix.md:65) and ADR-011 Decisions 6/7 publish this number as "10/10 completed with zero infrastructure failures".
findings.repro: Offline, no network, no spend: stub urlopen so every GET /tasks/<id> returns failure:env. Output: `[soak] 5/5 completed without an infrastructure failure`, report {'infrastructure_failures': 0, 'completed': 5, 'demo_ready': True, 'phases_seen': []}, row0 status=failure:env measured=False transport_error=None.
findings.acceptance: A run whose terminal record is not a real measurement (or at minimum `failure:env`) cannot count toward `completed` / `demo_ready`; the same case run through the eval set turns red before the fix and green after.

findings.claim: The phase taxonomy — the stated reason soak.py exists — mis-tags a read timeout that occurred *after* the POST landed, and a 200 with an unreadable body, as `1-client-could-not-connect`, the one distinction this repo has already established matters.
findings.evidence: evals/soak.py:102-108: only `urllib.error.HTTPError` maps to `2-server-rejected-or-not-ready`; every other exception falls to PHASE_CONNECT. `urllib` raises bare `TimeoutError` for a read timeout (request delivered, run may be executing) and `URLError` for a connect failure (nothing delivered) — evals/ablation.py:184-206 and docs/support-matrix.md:64 (D18) both depend on exactly that distinction. A JSON body the client cannot parse (ValueError) and a 200 without run_id (KeyError) also land in phase 1.
findings.repro: Three injected submit failures (TimeoutError / URLError / ValueError) all return phase='1-client-could-not-connect'.
findings.acceptance: `TimeoutError` (and any post-delivery failure) maps to a distinct phase from `URLError`; a case pins the exception->phase table so a future collapse turns red.

findings.claim: soak.py submits and polls through `ablation._http`, which silently retries connect-phase failures up to 3 times, so a transport failure that succeeded on retry leaves no trace in the report — "zero infrastructure failures, no transport error in any phase" is not readable off the artifact it cites.
findings.evidence: evals/soak.py:47 imports `_http`; evals/ablation.py:195-206 loops `for attempt in range(3)` over URLError with 5s/10s sleeps and neither prints nor returns the swallowed attempts. Connect-phase failures are precisely the D18 family the soak was written to observe. The committed reports contain no retry field, so their `infrastructure_failures: 0` cannot distinguish "no connect failure" from "connect failures that retried through".
findings.repro: One URLError injected on the first POST /tasks; report still {'infrastructure_failures': 0, 'demo_ready': True, 'phases_seen': []}, and 'URLError' in report_text is False.
findings.acceptance: Retried attempts are recorded per row (count + phase), and the published D20/ADR-011 sentence either reports them or the soak uses a non-retrying transport.

findings.claim: evals/soak.py — 206 new lines that produce every number in support-matrix D20 and ADR-011 Decisions 6 and 7 — has no eval case of any kind, while its sibling evals/ablation.py has three.
findings.evidence: grep -rl soak evals/golden evals/adversarial -> no matches. Compare ablation-preflight-refuses-old-build, ablation-env-failure-is-a-result, analysis-ablation-table-not-estimated. Consequence measured: R1, R2 and R3 are all live in the merged tree and the gate is 29/29 invariant + 93/93 fast, both green.
findings.repro: grep -rl soak evals/golden evals/adversarial; then .venv/bin/python -m evals.run --suite fast --no-report -> 93/93 with R1-R3 present.
findings.acceptance: A fast/invariant case drives soak.run_one/main against a stubbed transport and pins the exception->phase map and the demo_ready polarity; watched red against today's code.

findings.claim: This PR rewrote support-matrix D8 to publish "71.3-76.5s at M9 with five more cases", and the branch's own committed fast reports measure 79.0-79.8s with six more cases — a declared budget-breach number that its artifacts contradict, understating the breach by ~3.4s.
findings.evidence: docs/support-matrix.md:78 (added in this diff) vs ...-020310-fast.json wall_seconds 79.75, ...-021142 79.45, ...-145831 79.01, ...-162416 79.36 (all committed in this PR). The gap is the new case itself: readyz-tracks-the-run-slot costs 3.45s per its own got.run_seconds in every committed report, and the last pre-readyz run (20260820-220640-fast.json) was 75.83s. D8 is the row M12 in tasks/TODO.md is keyed to.
findings.repro: print wall_seconds from the committed fast reports -> [79.75, 79.36]; local re-run measured 79.55s.
findings.acceptance: D8 quotes the range its committed reports show (and the case count that produced it), or cites the report ids it was measured from.

findings.claim: README's case counts, edited in this PR, disagree with the runner and with the fast report committed in the same PR: it says 91 fast / 101 total, the runner says 93 fast / 103 files.
findings.evidence: README.md:38 ("offline gate: 91 cases") and README.md:228 ("it is 101 cases (91 of them in the offline gate)") vs [eval] suite 'fast': 93/93 and evals/report/20260821-162416-fast.json. Six new fast+invariant cases were added on this branch (main: 97 files / 87 fast, README on main said 96/86), so the edit added +5 and carried a pre-existing -1 forward.
findings.repro: .venv/bin/python -m evals.run --suite fast --no-report | tail -3 -> 93/93; ls evals/golden/*.json evals/adversarial/*.json | wc -l -> 103.
findings.acceptance: README numbers equal the runner's, and ideally are derived from a committed report rather than hand-counted.

findings.claim: The soak's `correct` column is not the repo's correctness metric: it uses raw string == instead of the production `verifier.answers_match` and drops the `status == "success"` requirement, yet its 8/10 -> 7/10 is published next to, and compared against, the ablation's answers_match-based cells.
findings.evidence: evals/soak.py:139 correct=bool(spec["answer"]) and str(answer).strip() == str(spec["answer"]).strip() vs evals/ablation.py:344 bool(rec.get("status") == "success" and answers_match(answer, spec["answer"])); docs/evals/evaluation-methodology.md defines correctness as "compared with the production verifier.answers_match". Two of the five soak tasks are currency answers where the rules diverge: answers_match('$39.00','39.00') is True, '$39.00'=='39.00' is False. ADR-011 Decision 7 point 1 cross-compares the two metrics directly.
findings.repro: from src.browser.verifier import answers_match; answers_match('$39.00','39.00') -> True; '$39.00'=='39.00' -> False.
findings.acceptance: soak uses answers_match and requires a successful terminal status, or D20/ADR-011 state explicitly that the soak's correctness rule is stricter and not comparable to the ablation's cells.

findings.claim: ADR-011 Decision 4's "Measured in the case: 5 ms, mid-run" is a number no committed report supports.
findings.evidence: specs/decisions/ADR-011-readiness-endpoint.md:75. The eight committed reports containing readyz-tracks-the-run-slot record during_latency_s of 0.001, 0.002, 0.002, 0.002, 0.003, 0.006, 0.007 — never 0.005 (local re-run: 0.006). The substance holds (all <=7 ms); the figure is unsourced.
findings.repro: grep -l readyz-tracks-the-run-slot evals/report/*.json and print got.during_latency_s.
findings.acceptance: The ADR quotes a value that appears in a named committed report, or states it as a range.

findings.claim: ADR-011 Decision 3's "Invariants, all graded" overstates: invariant 5 is not graded at all, and the graded ones only cover a single-submission happy path, so an implementation that sets ACTIVE_RUN before the semaphore is acquired stays green.
findings.evidence: specs/decisions/ADR-011-readiness-endpoint.md:58-67 vs src/browser/eval_adapter.py:823-851 — nothing asserts invariant 5, and no sample is taken with two submissions in flight. Ablation A8 (moving ACTIVE_RUN = run_id from inside `async with SEM` to submit_task-time) leaves the case PASSING. The author's seven-ablation claim DOES reproduce: all seven turn the case red.
findings.repro: Nine mutations applied to src/browser/server.py: A1-A7 RED, A8 PASS, A9 ERROR.
findings.acceptance: Either the ADR narrows "all graded" to the invariants the case actually asserts, or the case adds a second in-flight submission sample so active_run_id-when-not-busy is detectable.

findings.claim: "The event-loop candidate is now the weakest of the three ... measured ten times" rests on ten single instants, all taken ~2s after submission in runs lasting 4.7-13.7s, and all at a point where the run is provably inside an await.
findings.evidence: evals/soak.py:111-115 — mid is captured once, on the first poll iteration after a single time.sleep(2), and never resampled; run durations in evals/report/20260821-145535-soak.json are 4.71-13.73s. src/browser/agent.py:300-342 shows the first ~2s is async_playwright launch + navigate + observe + the awaited planner call. Both documents hedge ("narrowed, not eliminated"), which is why this is LOW.
findings.repro: Read evals/report/20260821-145535-soak.json: exactly one during.readyz sample per row, ten rows; compare with client_seconds.
findings.acceptance: Either the mid-run probe samples repeatedly across the run (and the report carries the series), or D20/ADR-011 D7 say "one probe per run, taken ~2s in" where they currently say "measured ten times".
